resale_co.name: Resale Certificate of Occupancy (Certificate of Occupancy for Transfer of Title)
resale_co.issued_by: Building & Zoning Office (the zoning officer inspects; the Construction Official signs off on any repairs)
resale_co.lead_time: The Borough approves or denies within 15 working days after a complete application is received
requirements: Complete application with the fee check; incomplete applications are not accepted
Current plot plan (survey) and a Flood Elevation Certificate; condos also need a Condo Certificate Survey
Zoning officer confirms the property is a permitted use or a valid nonconforming use under the Land Development Ordinance
Smoke alarms and carbon monoxide detectors on each floor, all working at the time of inspection
Fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen area (2014 form)
Unsafe conditions are referred to the Construction Official; the CO is issued only after required repairs are done
Leave keys with the application if the home is vacant; otherwise arrange access with the owner or tenant
A Declaration of Deed Restriction (use limited by FEMA flood regulations) must be filed for resale certificates and recorded with the Ocean County Clerk

fees.label: Resale Certificate of Occupancy, per residential dwelling unit
fees.quote: Check payable to the Borough of Ship Bottom in the amount of $50.00 per dwelling unit (commercial is $100.00 per unit), and must be submitted with the application.

fees.label: Re-inspection
fees.quote: If for any reason re-inspection is required there will an addition $25.00 fee will be assessed.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Resale Certificate of Occupancy and the 'Certificate of Occupancy for Transfer of Title' data form, attach a current survey and Flood Elevation Certificate, and submit them with a check payable to the Borough of Ship Bottom to the Building & Zoning Office, Borough Municipal Building, 1621 Long Beach Blvd. Also complete the Declaration of Deed Restriction for recording. Questions about resale certificates go to Matt Bernstein.
resale_co.contact_title: Code Enforcement & Trash and Recycling Coordinator (resale certificate contact)

evidence.quote: The Construction Official shall issue a Certificate of Occupancy only when the required repairs and/or other remedial action have been satisfactorily completed in compliance with the Uniform Construction Code.
See Section 1002.E.8.I and Section 1002.E.9 of the Land Development Ordinance for specific conditions of a temporary Certificate of Occupancy to permit transfer of title only.
The application will be approved or denied within fifteen (15) working days after receipt of a complete application.
CERTIFICATE OF OCCUPANCY FOR TRANSFER OF TITLE BOROUGH OF SHIP BOTTOM, OCEAN COUNTY, NEW JERSEY

Please note Deed Restrictions must be filed for all new construction, and resale certificates. Cases may vary for condominiums. For additional questions about resale certificates, please contact Matt Bernstein at (609) 494-2171 Ext. 131, or mbernstein@shipbottom.org.

authorities.how_to_apply: For Ship Bottom the County lists rental inspections only. If the Borough sends a seller to the County for a resale, the County process is: fill out the online application, the office calls to schedule, pay at the inspection (check payable to Ocean County Fire Marshal (OCFM), credit card or e-check; no cash).

fire_cert.notes: Not settled online. The July 2026 LEA registry lists the Ocean County Fire Marshal (C) as Ship Bottom's fire code enforcing agency, and the Borough's home page links 'Ocean County Fire Marshal Inspections'. But the County's Resale & Rental Home Inspections page lists Ship Bottom for 'Rentals for 1-2 family buildings' only, while it lists other towns for 'Resales and Rentals'. The Borough's own resale CO application requires working smoke and CO detectors on each floor and a fire extinguisher at the time of the zoning officer's inspection, so the Borough appears to cover resales itself, but no page says it issues the state certificate. If the County does inspect, its published fees are $45 (more than 10 business days), $90 (4 to 10 days) and $161 (3 days or less), not repeated here as Ship Bottom resale fees. The state directory (Ship Bottom is code 1528 there) lists Dennis Allen as county fire official. Ship Bottom Volunteer Fire Co. handles firefighting, not certificates.

other_items.label: Deed restriction
other_items.detail: A Declaration of Deed Restriction (FEMA flood rules; inspection of areas below base flood elevation on 48 hours notice) must be filed for resale certificates and recorded with the Ocean County Clerk. Condominiums may differ.

other_items.label: Survey and flood elevation certificate
other_items.detail: The resale CO application must include a current plot plan (survey) and a Flood Elevation Certificate; condos need a Condo Certificate Survey.

other_items.label: Temporary CO for transfer of title
other_items.detail: The form refers to Land Development Ordinance Sections 1002.E.8.I and 1002.E.9 for a temporary Certificate of Occupancy that permits transfer of title only.
